utterances.text: We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw here that the Prosecutor Ms. Gustafson is alleging once again, as in the indictment, as if nothing had happened, as if all this evidence had not been called. She claims that President Karadzic ordered the cessation of the alleged shelling of Sarajevo only after Markale 1994 and because of pressure exerted by NATO, and that it was only then that he ordered the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps to respond to fire from the BH army, applying a 1:1 ratio. That is absolutely incorrect as well, because already on the 14th of January, 1994, that is to say, three weeks before the incident at Markale, President Karadzic at a meeting with the representatives of the army and the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, as noted down by General Mladic in his notes, P1484 on page 149, he ordered that 1:1 should be the ratio of responding to fire, irrespective of any NATO pressure. I would like to remind the Chamber that the leadership and the authorities of Republika Srpska had a very negative position regarding the targeting of civilian areas in town. Even Djeric did that because Karadzic did not have a command function at the time. There was this ban on directing artillery fire at the city all the way up until the end of the war. Many, many orders not to fire unless it is absolutely necessary. Ms. Gustafson also said that Gengo, Sladoje, and General Milosevic as Defence witnesses confirmed that they did not take any cautionary measures when they opened fire at the city. This is what the witnesses actually said on transcript pages that were quoted by Ms. Gustafson. Gengo on T29781. I'm going to read it out in English. [In English] "First of all, fire was never opened if it was not a response to enemy attack. When we were under attack I used 120- and 80-millimetre mortars. I did not need to use them at any other time. So when we opened fire, it was in response to the enemy fire that had been opened at us. If they had opened fire from a settlement, they knew what we -- that we would respond, so they should have taken measures in order to avoid civilian casualties. I could not see whether there were any civilian people around that firing position or not. All I did was to return fire on the firing position from which fire had been opened on us." [Interpretation] There were references made to the testimony of certain witnesses to the effect that there was not an instant response. Rather, a mortar would be moved and only then the Serbs would respond. However, if the OTP had a proper military expert, I would tell them that time was needed to calculate co-ordinates, and as for a firing point, it had to be located and then the elements would have to be communicated, and only then could a response follow. As for Sladoje, Ms. Gustafson says that he said something that he did not say, transcript page 30573. This is what he said: [In English] "There were soldiers in each and every neighbourhood. The civilian population lived in Nedzarici," Serbian settlement. [Interpretation] I inserted that "Serbian settlement." [In English] "There was the barracks there. There was this unity of the army and the civilian population because impossible to live in any other way. That is to say that not a single neighbourhood was civilian only. It is a neighbourhood where people live, but also the military was stationed there and that is practically the way it is in the all urban areas where there was a military presence. How can you expect us not to open fire if our positions are jeopardised? And the other side includes both civilians and soldiers. They are both present there, so it is the soldiers who are firing at us that are jeopardising the civilians on both sides -- on that side" -- [Interpretation] I can add "on both sides." Now, just look at how big Sarajevo is, look at its surface. And it is very fortunate that the Trial Chamber visited Sarajevo. There are civilians living throughout this urban area; however, not all points were targeted. There were many neighbourhoods where a shell never fell. Why did the OTP not make an effort to see why Bjelave was not fired at, why different neighbourhoods were not fired at where Muslims and Serbs live as well or predominantly Muslims. Why? Because nobody was shooting at us from there. We heard a Defence witness here who confirmed that there were almost 300 mosques in Sarajevo and that they're full, especially on Fridays, and no one ever targeted any one of them and I think that somebody from the Trial Chamber asked why not. And they said because they were not firing from there. I would like to remind the Trial Chamber that there are many gasoline stations in Sarajevo. Not a single one was ever targeted. Witnesses of the United Nations spoke here -- actually, we saw a document of the Muslim army. They were wondering how it was that people lived in Sarajevo, that they were walking about, living that kind of life although there was a war going on. That was possible, Excellencies, because if they did not shoot, the Serbs would not respond. Witnesses from the UN say Karadzic had all of that under his control. When an agreement would be reached on a cease-fire or anti-sniping agreement, for a long time there would be no fire. I'm going to tell you why. Because once an agreement is reached and when somebody is observing the Muslim side, they do not dare violate the cease-fire. And when appeals are issued, the Serbs make promises and declare a unilateral cease-fire and the Muslim side fires and forces Serbs into responding. So that was not true about Sladoje. General Milosevic on transcript page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the transcript page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Said the following: [In English] "We were not allowed to shell a civilian area" -- [Interpretation] The page is T32582. [In English] "We were not allowed to shell a civilian area nor indeed would we have chosen to shell a civilian area. The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps didn't do that. Wherever there were civilians, that meant that was not a target for us. We never fired at those areas." [Interpretation] Towards the end of this session, I will show you that close to 6.000 victims in Sarajevo were combatants. Only in Stari Grad municipality - held 90 per cent by Serbs and Bascarsija held 10 per cent by the Muslims - had 680 combatants killed, mostly in 1992. And there are about 1.002 cases where the same victims are shown in more than one list, and about 4 per cent of them out of those 1.002 are civilians, not the reverse, as was portrayed here. On page T33123, General Milosevic clearly explained what principles guided the SRK if there was a danger of civilian casualties when responding to fire the army: [In English] "If there is a civilian there, it is deemed a civilian area. But if fire is opened from that area, then an assessment will have to be made what to do with the -- with that target which then constituted a military target. There would be a solution. There would be a procedure put in place not to put civilians in danger when it's possible. If it's not, then an absolute assessment will have to be made if there would be collateral damage which would outweigh a military mission to be accomplished, then this is abandoned." [Interpretation] You have seen those officers. It is a sin before God that Milosevic and Galic were convicted. You have seen their subordinate commanders who are decent people and trained officers. Ms. Gustafson, on page 24 on the second day of the closing arguments, thought she had caught the Defence in a contradiction. It is said that soldiers were trained in humanitarian law and she says -- or rather, we claim that they were untrained. Trained in using weapons is one thing and trained in humanitarian law is a different thing. Only officers in our system were trained as officers, including humanitarian law, not all the troops. Ms. Gustafson stated that only one document out of the 100 mentioned in paragraphs 2392 to 2394 of our final brief referred to fire opened from Kosevo Hospital by ABH; but in D2798, it says that ABH fired six 82-millimetre mortar shells from Kosevo, or D507, shown to General Razek, a video-clip of the statement of Lord Owen about ABH opening fire from the Kosevo Hospital. And documents cited in paragraph 1955 of our final brief mention mortar fire from many other civilian buildings, not only the hospital. And such things happened every time there would be a lull and Sarajevo disappeared from the front pages and headlines in international media. Ms. Gustafson stated that Defence witness Veljovic confirmed that air bombs were imprecise but the same witness stated on page 2986: [In English] "Thank you. Were you involved in the work that was carried out on building the modified aerial bombs? "A. I'm not competent for such things. I am an infantry officer. I don't know anything about rocket mortars, metals, and so on and so forth. I did not participate in that. I am not an expert on such matters. I am not a technical expert by profession. "Q. Thank you. And you are not a ballistics expert either, are you? Do you have any ballistics training? "A. No, I don't." [Interpretation] The page was T29286. Ms. Gustafson said that in order to develop a new piece of combat equipment eight or ten years are required. This is not a new combat asset. It's about changing the warhead on one rocket with another, using four different engines with different performances, and it's all about calculating the pressure of the engines to that warhead and its thrust, and testing it on Zuc, or rather, testing ground, as one protected witness of the Prosecution said here, that they were tried and tested before being used at Zuc. Speaking of imprecision, the imprecision of this weapon, in another case which is still pending, the Judge told the witness not to exaggerate when he said that these bombs were more precise when dropped from an airplane than when they are launched from launchers with tested engines. Regardless of that, let us see how many victims resulted from the use of this weapon, how many times was it used in an urban area. It was always a large military installation that was the target. Andja Gotovac confirmed that her house was not targeted. It missed the Miskin Crni weapon factory by a few centimetres and the bomb fell on the road. Let alone the case of the school in Hrasnica, about which KDZ --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the number of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was the first one to get to the school and the first time he didn't see either rocket motors, just an old woman, no soldiers. And the next day he came, he was served completely different evidence. That is an investigation that Berko Zecevic started again 12 years later to establish that it was the way he said it was. Berko Zecevic was -- Mile Poparic, expert witness, on page T32 -- 39042 to 43, said that such a weapon could be developed within eight months, six to eight months, and perhaps six months is more realistic considering that already-known assets were used to make that weapon. First of all, neither Allsop or other UNPROFOR investigators were able to establish the angle of descent and it's not possible for Zecevic's deviations or error of margin to be acceptable. Zecevic determined that at Markale, one angle of descent was 60 degrees, plus/minus 5. If we accept that the angle of descent of a shell can be determined based on the position of the stabiliser, as Berko Zecevic did the next day, with a margin of error of 33 per cent and Allsop agreed, as Ms. Gustafson said, and based on that, she claims that Allsop confirmed Berko's finding, then the possible error of 33 per cent in a degree of 60 per cent would be 19.8. So the angle of descent of a shell could be less than 19.8 degrees or even higher than 60 degrees by 19.8. It is a huge range. It means practically that the shell could have been fired by anybody but the Chinese. And it has a maximum angle of descent of 55.3 and the minimal 47.3, so that range is less than 30 degrees all in all. In the record, it should be 85, line 11: [In English] The maximum angle of descent is 55.3. [Interpretation] No. The maximal is 85.3, that's from a close range, and the minimal angle of descent is 47.3. Luckily the Trial Chamber has been at Markale and they saw for themselves. How probable is it that it was done without calculating the target and without deliberate intent? I leave it to the Trial Chamber to judge. This Court, which is a UN Court, and this Office of the Prosecutor, which was appointed by the United Nations, neglect several official findings of the United Nations regarding Markale I and they take into account and rely on the findings of Berko Zecevic, a high official of the war industry of Bosnia-Herzegovina, who volunteered not to find but to prove who had fired. And this is the same man who was denied access to the UN investigation by Mr. Hamill, a high UN official. It is not all right for the parties to the conflict to participate in the investigation, especially if there is no third party. How can a Chamber trust Berko Zecevic and convict General Galic for this incident and set aside everything that UN officers found and reported about that incident? I don't know when the break is. I don't have much more time and I have a lot to present. Let me just say that the Office of the Prosecutor withdrew from the claims of Berko Zecevic that those were air bombs, although he claims that those were aerosol bombs. He is either lying or he is -- [In English] Fuel air bombs. [Interpretation] Fuel air bombs. They create quite different destruction, different injuries. It's absolutely out of the question that they were ever used. And the Office of the Prosecutor accepts that this was a lie, that it cannot be believed, but they did accept Berko Zecevic's claims in every other respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for 20 minutes and resume at 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I was informed that you have one hour and ten minutes to conclude your closing arguments. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Sorry. I said I would be very happy if this ten could be extended to 20 or something like that but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think so. Please conclude in the time allotted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] I shall try to condense our final brief, the Defence final brief. Everything is in the final brief, Defence final brief, but I have to refer to this incredible selectivity of the Prosecution when they quote the entire document except for the last line in a document which clearly defines its character. For instance, when I'm asked what targets and I said "only military targets," this is omitted, for instance, and a multitude of other things. The Prosecution wants what they stated in paragraphs 608 and 609 and 614 to 616, they want that to stand which is that there was a policy of terror in Sarajevo. Without any obligation on their part to ascertain who created this policy of terror, what its components were, what proves its existence. And they give a totally erroneous motive and cause. It is quite clear that the only side which could benefit from the suffering of Sarajevo and the citizens of Sarajevo, both Muslim and Serb ethnicity, was the Muslim political side. They took advantage of this, they drew benefits from it. The Serbian did not have any benefit from that. Excellencies, in the exhibits you have ample evidence where you can see from the beginning that initially I believed the foreigners very much and I actually criticised the Army of Republika Srpska without justification. Had there existed any agreement or any plan and policy of terror, all of them would have told me, because they were not afraid of me: Come on, don't play the fool, this is what we agreed upon. But never in any intercept is there any insincerity in our efforts for Sarajevo not to suffer. But this is just unsustainable, I mean the way it is portrayed. I should like to refer the Chamber's attention to 40 witnesses from the SRK who talked here, who testified here, annulling everything that the Prosecution charges me with. And the documents P1478 which are mis-characterised by the Prosecution, that is pages 73 to 74, then P1 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please slow down with the numbers. We cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please slow down when you refer to the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So paragraphs of the Prosecution final brief 608 and 609 and paragraphs from 614 to 616. The Prosecution sustains this thesis about the existence of a policy of terror in Sarajevo and it invokes selectively documents, omitting from those documents the key elements which actually determine the nature, the character, of such documents. The documents which I recommend to the Chamber, so not to take their word for it but to see and to check, these are the documents which have been misquoted: P1478, pages 173 to 174; then P991; P5989; D4373, paragraphs 5 and 7; P1484, pages 140 and 141 and 149, all these are mis-characterisations. Then P1006, D324, P5065, P6297. In all these documents, authentic documents, secret documents between the commands, they all refer to the protection of civilians in Sarajevo whenever action is carried out, and they clearly show that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina is where it is and where the hideouts in the city are and where action has to be taken. So the Prosecution simply invokes documents that have not been accepted, like P4800 and 4807, in footnotes 2291, 2294, and 2311. This is what you have to resort to if you have to patch up some hollow proofs and evidence. Then in paragraph 619 they say that Karadzic received regular reports on the situation in Sarajevo. So what? Did those reports contain any proof that I was informed about crimes committed by Serbs and then I was papering over that, I was keeping silent. These documents refer exclusively to events, to developments, to attacks. The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina attacked here or there and we responded in this or that way. These are secret reports, and all stories about how the Serbs fired a shell would have been recorded there. And the observers of the observation posts, the Limas would have been informed because they were informed in advance of any intention and targets. The Prosecution failed to demonstrate that any specific incidents were something Karadzic was aware of or had been informed about. And in fact many of the incidents that are in the indictment were incidents in respect to which UNPROFOR did not protest with the Sarajevo government. Simply, there was no protest for specific incidents because UNPROFOR was not satisfied that it was so. In paragraph 621, the document which the Prosecution erroneously quotes, misquotes, is P2493, page 9. They leave out the key word which is that retaliation shall be against military targets. You can see the handwriting here, the annotation. [In English] "Retaliation is productive. When they shell Doboj, we retaliate. It is effective. "Q. Civilian targets? "Karadzic: No, military targets." [Interpretation] There is not a single shred of evidence about any reprisals taken against someone who was not opening fire, and there is no proof about deliberate and intentional, conscious targeting of civilian targets, and Karadzic did not direct terror as in paragraph 622 and as can be seen from evidence about humanitarian proof. Our paragraphs 1324 and 1325 and 2984 and 2988 explain this question. The Prosecutor's invoking some secondary sources of people who are not in the know about how allegedly Karadzic had said something or how they had understood something that Karadzic had said is of no relevance. It cannot be of any importance in respect of the documents having regard to the documents I sent to the army. I was the only supreme commander who was restraining the army, and my conflicts with the army were not because of some crimes which they committed or mine own; it was actually a fight for them to let through humanitarian relief. Here you say that Karadzic manages -- managed the crisis by managing humanitarian relief. I interfered with humanitarian relief only when so requested by the representatives of the international community, and Sadako Ogata thanked me courteously many times. I personally went to Bratunac to convince not the army, not the troops, but the people to let humanitarian convoys through. Over 20.000 landings of humanitarian aircraft at Sarajevo airport, which was our territory that we, of course, handed over for that particular purpose, were carried out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (redacted). Some of them, about 10 or 20 per cent, did encounter some difficulties. But when we talk about Srebrenica, you will see that this was not the way it was; namely, they did have enough food. Never did Karadzic deal with that, except in the form of encouraging and ordering that it be made possible. Of course this is falsified by the Prosecution because they omit to say that I said when the airport is shut off, of course humanitarian convoys can still use that route. This was omitted from the account of the Prosecution. And who is this supposed to deceive? Exclusively the Trial Chamber and to lead the Trial Chamber to adopt an erroneous decision. This is document P859, where they say because of the abuse of 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina smuggling of arms, et cetera, Karadzic states that humanitarian relief can still use alternative routes, but the airport shall be shut down for these reasons. [In English] "Of course, humanitarian convoys are free to utilise the earlier routes across our territory." [Interpretation] This is not in the presentation of Prosecution in their brief. In paragraph 628, it is claimed that I had been informed, that I had agreed that the Serbian response was inadequate. I am not competent there. I thought that the proportional response was 1:1. I always quarrelled with the army and they were right. I was not right, because I believed these foreigners and I spent more time with the foreigners than doing my own presidential job. Foreigners were always visiting me or I was abroad at conferences and I addressed these issues only when so requested. I believed that our responses were inadequate, but they were not inadequate. Under the law the president cannot order a unit that has been attacked not to respond. No one can prevent a soldier from defending himself. That just doesn't exist. And with the support of the international community and the media, it was easy for the Muslim army, not to say the Muslims, to endure -- under pressure, to shoot at us, get firing response and then they report us. I did think that there was some senseless shelling, but when the army showed me what had actually happened, I was proven wrong. Excellencies, it is [indiscernible] here, the contention of the Prosecution is that there had existed a plan of terrorisation, a plan and a decision to terrorise. Also a permit or perhaps order to snipe at civilians. Look at what the Prosecution has charged me with. There is not a single fatality which has been properly processed from sniping. They question the credibility of Mile Poparic and Dr. Subotic. They are actually academicians in respect of what the Prosecution experts did. They have shown and demonstrated everything. It is absolutely impossible to hit someone with a sniper from a thousand metres' distance. They didn't show where Munira Zametica was, was she turned towards the creek or facing away from the creek. They didn't show that. Everything depends on that. They didn't demonstrate whether you could shoot from the left bank by the church in the river Dobrinja. Sanija Dzevlan herself saw ricochetted automatic fire bullets from the asphalt and here it is claimed that she was hit in the lower end of the -- lower part of the back, but this is nonsense. This is an insult to the Trial Chamber first and foremost. At Baba Stijena, between the place where the little Pita was wounded and Baba Stijena, there is a hill. Whether there are houses or woods, that's irrelevant, but there was a hill there. You cannot from a pointed rock hit someone with a sniper with precision from a distance of 1.000 or 1500 metres. This is pure nonsense. And if the Prosecution hopes that this will actually pass, we have nothing to say. Mile Poparic, Zorica Subotic all stated facts here, and it is not an isolated belief that there was a planned explosion at Markale. You heard the investigator say: Let's go to the roof to see whether the stabiliser is perhaps not on the roof, et cetera. But the facts which were adduced here that is firm as a rocket cannot be refuted. It is an exercise in futility. Let me show you a couple of photographs at this point so that you can see how things actually look. This is Dresden after the Second World War. This is Gaza --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Are they in our evidence, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I would just like to illustrate my point. I don't want to tender it. I should like to illustrate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't see the point of your presenting documents which are not in our evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, this is Mostar after three wars into -- three months into the war. And there is not a single dent in Sarajevo. Just Unis buildings, government buildings, Holiday Inn, and Rainbow building were mentioned, and we have proof that they also opened fire from there. There is not a single dent on the buildings. They say that we had a policy of terror and policy of killing over 1260 days of the war. Where are these victims? 6.000 of them are combatants and fighters, most of them. Where are the victims? The victims which are impressive, or rather, the large numbers is the ones that they caused at Markale and in the queue for humanitarian relief and the queue for water. These are -- in document, rather, D1115, which is a document of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina where they give the names of military victims of combatants, casualties. They are in Sarajevo. The total is between 10.000 to 74.000. It is about 60.000. The total number of cases in Bosnia and Herzegovina is 98.000, and of that, Serbs account for about 30.000 and Muslim soldiers for about 60.000. And that is the real figure. And when you do your deliberations, we will have a population census result already. On this list of the 5.800 combatants killed in Sarajevo proper, there are overlaps, there are cases of same combatants reported twice or sometimes even thrice or four times. And these overlaps or double -- figures reported twice, there are 1.002 such cases. Of the 5.800, 1.002 combatants are shown in two places in different times. So these are the victims which were shown as civilian victims whenever it was required. God will not forgive us such lies, and one should believe that God knows all this, because the Serbian side tried to reduce the number of victims to the minimum. Document D1115 that we got from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was compared with document P5008. This is a document concerning the number of victims in Sarajevo. There are only a few civilians there, only a few. There are 19 civilians in all those overlaps, so that's about 4 per cent if we look at the 1.002 as well. So that is how one manipulates figures and that is how one manipulates accusations that I can understand in times of war and for propaganda purposes, but one should not appear before a distinguished court of law in that way. Another thing, the most terrible weapon as far as civilians are concerned is a multiple rocket-launcher. It would create chaos in streets. It is the most catastrophic weapon. The Serb army never fired multiple rocket-launchers at an urban area. You saw these officers and generals, how properly they treated their work and also their fellow citizens of any religious affiliation. Your Excellencies, does this mean that -- well, actually although these documents were admitted, this was done on the basis of documents. Can I show the piece that has to do with the militarisation of Sarajevo or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow. It's up to you how to present the documents during your closing argument. If it is in our evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Documents on the basis of which this was done, they were admitted; however, this is visual, this is on a map, Google Earth. It shows where these positions are and -- before that, briefly, I would just like to present paragraph 634 of the Prosecution brief to you as well as 621. There are extremely selective quotations from a document as if Karadzic were supporting this. [In English] "That maybe some of our gunners have bad eyes." [Interpretation] This is the kind of cynicism that I have never displayed in my life and I abhor that kind of thinking. Please take a look at this document and see what it looks like. Karadzic, in that document, on page 9, says civilians are not the target, they're only military targets. When the Prosecution says they were trained -- and I've already said that they were trained in the laws of war but not how to handle artillery pieces that they perhaps handled when doing their term in the military 15 years before that. In paragraph 635, it says that Karadzic responded with threats, for example, to General Smith in May 1995. It wasn't Karadzic that was issuing the threats; it was Smith. And he asked for the bombing of the Serbs, not the Muslims who had started the initiative -- the offensive. I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to put all these documents in their proper context. If something happened after July in Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Please bear in mind that this document, i.e., visual aid, you are using to assist your closing argument is not part of the documents. So bear in mind to make a correct reference for the future purpose. For example, in relation to the previous paragraph, the Prosecution final brief 634, you seem to have referred to Banbury's handwritten note page 9, but in the transcript it appears that you said "in that document on page 9." So later on when we read this document, closing argument, we have no idea what document you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I was referring to P2493.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, which is Banbury's handwritten note; we saw it before. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Very well. Then in P2264, it is not Karadzic that is threatening General Smith; it's the other way around. Serbs, official, serious Serbs, never issued any threats because they were not in a position to threaten anyone. We're not that kind of power to be able to threaten anyone. On the other hand, it was clear to UNPROFOR and everyone else that NATO is one thing and that they were a different thing until they united. When NATO started their strikes, upon their instructions, then they became one and the same thing. Allow me to show the degree of militarisation of Sarajevo. All of that is based on the documents that have already been admitted. The imagery would be a lot richer if we were to include all the documents that were admitted later on because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When we went through exercises such as this during the course of trial, they were submitted to the Prosecution in advance so efforts could be made to determine any responses we had vis-à-vis their accuracy, reliability, and so on. It's not the time to create new exhibits and present them to the Court during closing. If they're grounded on evidence, as the Court noted, of course that's fine; but this appears to be something quite new.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber agrees with Mr. Tieger. Mr. Karadzic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm not going to insist, but this is not a new exhibit. This is just a presentation of evidence that has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, it's just a waste of time. Just please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Robinson dealt with the question of Srebrenica better than I would have. The Prosecution asserts that there was this kind of plan or that kind of plan in terms of what would happen in Srebrenica. For an entire year, the Serb side tolerated the existence of large areas in Podrinje, the Drina Valley, under the control of the Muslim forces that were mixed with the Muslim population and they are taking advantage of the population and taking advantage of their homes. When our people would advance, they would run away; and when our people would retreat, then they would go back to these houses and they would fire at us. And then they say that -- Zivanovic said that this was not the destruction of property but of military facilities. Ms. Gustafson said that I ordered, that we ordered, in the autumn of 1992, that Srebrenica be taken. We were compelled to go for Srebrenica in the spring of 1993. Why do we not do that earlier on? Because we expected a map on the basis of which the Muslims would get a significant part of Podrinje, the Drina Valley. So that is the reason why Srebrenica was in 1993, not in 1992. I've already said that I issued this order on the 16th of March and they are overlooking the fact that it contains a lot of content that no one asked me for and that is favourable for civilians, especially Muslim civilians, because at that moment, all my orders about protecting civilians exclusively pertain to Muslim civilians because at the moment when Srebrenica fell, there were no Serb civilians in Srebrenica. Just one more thing in relation to Sarajevo and everything else. I would like to draw your attention to the following, the attention of the Trial Chamber to the following, that many incidents, massive ones, bloody incidents happened when I was attending international conferences, and that's the only reason why I went abroad. That would happen, these incidents were calculated, they wanted the conferences to be disrupted and interrupted. I just wonder about Koricanske Stijene, whether there was this awareness that I was at the conference in London; however, the Prosecution does know that the Minister of the Interior, Mico Stanisic, who is an extremely honest man and very well-aware of the law and he was acquitted on account of Koricanske Stijene, whereas the OTP insists that I'm responsible for Koricanske Stijene. They say that I co-operated with Momo Mandic. Momo Mandic, before the court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a court before which it is very hard for a Serb to fare well, he was set free. He was acquitted. Gojko Klickovic was acquitted as well. There is the prime minister, there is the ministers, the local leadership. How can the president of the republic be responsible for that then? These are things that a normal person cannot understand. Most of these incidents from the 27th of March -- no, 27th of May, when I was in Lisbon, that's when they interrupted our negotiations because of this alleged mortar shell in the street of Vase Miskin, which certainly could not have been a Serb shell because it is such a narrow street that would have to hit one of the walls, I mean, of the buildings in that street, that is. As far as Srebrenica is concerned, Srebrenica and Zepa had lost the status of safe areas already in May, the agreement was signed on the 8th of May, and according to all international agreements nobody was supposed to fire from Srebrenica, nobody. And it's not only that they were shooting but they were going out whenever they felt like it. They made necklaces of Serb ears and they showed this to foreigners. They would steal cattle, 100 sheep. They killed all the Serb civilians that they would find in the villages around Srebrenica. And here it is being asserted that Srebrenica was starved. KDZ45 said how big his farm was. He's not the only one. They all had that much. 5- or 6.000 inhabitants lived in the town of Srebrenica itself and several thousand refugees from neighbouring municipalities; whereas Christine Schmitz testified in this case and stated that on the 25th or 27th of June, 1995, as an experienced humanitarian worker she entered Srebrenica and she observed the children because she said that nothing can be put falsely as far as children are concerned. Then she saw the children playing in the street and they looked healthy and they looked fine. So if children are playing in the street, that means that there is no shooting; and if they're not malnourished, if they're healthy, that means that there is enough food and there is enough medicine. The Prosecution probably regretted the fact that they received that answer. So we tolerated these terrible losses that were inflicted upon us by the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The commanders of this division have blood up to their shoulders. They are direct killers and some of them were acquitted before this court. And ultimately we had to separate Zepa and Srebrenica and that was the main task. It wasn't Karadzic who ordered on the 9th to attack Srebrenica; rather, he agreed that Srebrenica be taken because Srebrenica had stopped defending itself. On that day, in the morning, Suljic, the president of the municipality, called Sarajevo and asked for permission to withdraw because the army would not defend Srebrenica. Krstic, in the evening, called the Main Staff and he said that the conditions were right for him to enter Srebrenica and I agreed to that with many provisos, all the things that they had to take care of and so on and so forth. Also, most importantly, people did not think that the army would enter. We have this intercept from the 10th and Muslims are saying: It seems that the Chetniks do not wish to enter Srebrenica. Now, what happened when they entered Srebrenica? I saw a few killings of some people who happened to be there by members of that well-known platoon and the members of this platoon took part in the killing of POWs. The population had left earlier on. They left of their own free will. They went to the base in Potocari. We have evidence to the effect that Serb shells were falling around the area, not on them. It was corroborated through testimony here that they had M-84, the best tank in the world, the Serbs did. But it -- it's the best tank in the world but it did not hit the hospital, the school, or the civilians. They didn't want the civilian population to disperse in the woods. There was no encounter between the army and the population. And then you have all this evidence about me not believing, not knowing whether we had taken it or not. And I'm asking Deronjic: Is it correct that we have entered Srebrenica? Which is ridiculous that the supreme commander should ask some civilian: Have we entered Srebrenica? But that's what the situation was like. And then there was this feverish activity in terms of providing security for these civilians. No one had any idea of the remaining people not surrendering. 10- to 15.000 people were scattered through the forest -- actually, they had set out in this column. The Serb side was the last one that agreed to the evacuation of civilians, the last one. Mladic gave that only on the morning of the 12th. There is no way that there was a deportation. It was understandable that those who were not from Srebrenica would leave, but it did not cross our minds that the local population would leave. And then in the media there are reports saying 8.000 - I don't know how many thousand - civilians in Srebrenica were shot dead. And of course I'm calling Deronjic and asking him what all of that was about. I did not install Deronjic or Brdjanin, as was stated here in these arguments presented here orally, I did not install anyone. They were elected there. If the people wanted them there, then they were elected there and appointed there. Then I asked Deronjic: What's all this talk about killings? And he says to me: Nothing, President, lies as always. Just as he said to Vice-President Koljevic towards the end of August: They're lying, nothing happened in Srebrenica. Nothing did happen in Srebrenica. My attention is being drawn to Srebrenica and to civilians, and whatever is happening happened 80 to 100 kilometres away from Srebrenica and it wasn't happening to civilians. And of course when we got the first convincing evidence, these mortal remains on the surface, when Madeleine Albright found this, then there were orders to investigate that and the military prosecutor said no one knows anything about this and no one wants to know anything about this. There was an immediate response. Why am I saying -- I don't want to go into the part why it is not genocide. Mr. Robinson did that better. Why am I saying that not everybody who was exhumed had been executed. For instance, P4841 is the list of those exhumed in Zvornik. We received that from -- out of 4.415, 2.290 were exhumed in Zvornik. If you analyse this, out of these 2.000-something, 79 were -- had died before 1995, but they were all found together in one grave, not in separate ones like Janc said. Out of the remaining number, who did go missing in 1995, 1.500 have been established to have been killed in this breakout by combat -- in fact, 1.200 were killed during the breakout. And 3.000 were killed at locations that we know as locations of surrender. There are mistakes in the record but out of 2.299 exhumed in Zvornik, 799 were -- died before 1995. And out of 1500 who were killed in 1995, 1200 were killed during the breakout. And 3.000 went missing at places that we know as locations of surrender or were last seen there. I cannot show you other analyses now because the situation is not right, but other analyses -- the previous figure is not 3.000, it is 300 went missing or were last seen at places that we know as locations of surrender, surrender to the Army of Republika Srpska. In a document from ICMP, I found thousands of people who are recorded in ICMP documents and the BH army as having been killed either before July 1995 or in other places. Thousands. In a sample of 300, a random sample of 300, 16 per cent are false, 16 per cent at least were not killed at that time. And we have evidence for that. If this work were to be done properly, the figure should be higher. So that this story and the leading of evidence about the number of those killed is far from good and would certainly affect the qualification. What matters is to establish the truth. The OTP believes that the Trial Chamber will latch on to any sentence that would enable them to convict. If they believe that, then it's not about finding out the truth. But for the sake of international sanity, we must be about establishing the truth. We must not mutilate documents or put false evidence before the Court. We don't know in which direction this world is heading, but I believe in a very bad direction. All these trials, without us being aware of it, are part of this bad direction in which we are heading. It's a shame that this is not a trial by jury because the OTP would fare better. Such courts do not judge the accused. They judge the skills of the parties, whereas the accused sits there like a potted flower just listening. So if this was a trial by jury, Mr. Tieger would easily win against me. However, I'm interested in the truth, regardless of what my fate will be and that truth frees me of every responsibility except for the moral one and I do feel moral responsibility because I'm sorry for everyone who was killed there. And you can find it in my documents when I said I'm happy that we haven't been waging war for one year now with the Croats. Can you imagine how many of our and their boys are still alive thanks to that. Now, speaking about the merits, the essence. None of my generals or ministers should even have been indicted, let alone convicted and sentenced to very long terms of imprisonment. It is justice that was condemned. Out of those people, many of them were acquitted before a BH court which is much harsher than this one. The number of victims is exaggerated in this and many other courts and the military structure and civilian structures were falsely represented. These things can be used for propaganda but not before a court of law. In these documents, for instance, we have several that show that. Just for example they talk about Dusan Janc here. Dusan Janc himself says that he excluded a large number of cases because he didn't know how they came to be there, how they came to be included. Very renowned experts of the Prosecution say: Well, nobody told us there was any fighting before July 1995. One expert says: Well, I established they had to be killed after the taking of Srebrenica because if they had been killed before, then they would have been found dead in Srebrenica. That is the extent of their ignorance. They believe that everybody who was killed or exhumed was killed after Srebrenica. And over the four years -- I will now read to you from a document that relates to ten municipalities in the area of Podrinje, where a total of 8.000-plus people were exhumed year by year. I believe it's 229 -- D2229. You see, in this report we see the figure that the Muslim side had made an overview of all those exhumed, all those killed throughout the war in ten municipalities. And that shows that 1.313 corpses were in individual graves. And it is highly unlikely they were victims of mass executions. About 15 were found in group graves, which is the term when the grave contains up to five persons; and the rest were found in mass graves, which, as we saw clearly from other exhibits, were used for multiple burials of people who died or were killed in 1992, in 1993, 1994, and 1995. And these things were built into the indictment against me and against Serbs in general. So the number has not been established and it should not find its way into any judgement as an established number because it hasn't been. And there is convincing evidence that people were killed between 1992 and 1995 and buried more or less in the same places. Erdemovic also testified that he had been informed that in Branjevo there had been burials earlier during the war. So it's perfectly clear this has to be subjected to a new analysis and reconsideration. If I could only show you now what is marked in a special colour those who were not killed or died during -- I can read it to you. P4841 is the exhibit showing deaths in other places and there are other documents, P4843. These exhibits are either in the documents of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Janc himself says that the family reported the man missing in 1992. How come he's in this grave? Well, the easy answer is: Multiple burials. Or judgements from the courts of Bosnia-Herzegovina in that area and district courts. D229. That's the one I'm trying to open now. The number of persons found in other locations or have been established to have been killed at a different time is very high and coming close to 50 per cent of the number used by the Prosecution and featuring in the indictment. And it's not a small error. Even in the sample of 300 chosen randomly by the ICMP, almost 60 per cent are false and we can prove that. And we could prove much more than that if we had the chance. If it turns up in one list, 500 mortal remains, DNA identified profiles, but nobody can identify the person because nobody's looking for him, nobody reported him as missing, then it's more than clear that person did not get killed in 1995. God knows when he died and was buried wherever he died. And it's perfectly understandable that nobody will bury him on his own property; they will take him to a known burial place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid we are not getting any English translation. Yes, please repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have not been hearing anything since the last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is your microphone on?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, sometimes it's the bucket missing, sometimes there's no water. This whole evidence, if the documents are not mutilated, if they are taking -- taken into account in its entirety and if they're ever analysed by professionals, I have no doubt about the outcome of this trial. No doubt at all. I will be acquitted and several other judgements will be revised because some people should never have been convicted, because Galic was convicted by a Chamber that neglected the evidence of qualified UN officers and relied on an interested party, Berko Zecevic. There is no evidence for the allegation of -- for the alleged JCE. When the war began, if we are offering everyone to establish their own municipalities wherever possible, it's not possible for a joint criminal enterprise to exist, it's not possible to dislocate these people. The proof of that is that in Republika Srpska you will find more places that are purely Muslim, such as Bosanski Dubocac, Bosanski Kobas, Janja. Janja is not purely Muslim but it is overwhelmingly Muslim. Not a single village like that can be found in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina in August 1995 or after 1992. We did not drive our Muslims out and the Croats were involved in our army until the end of the war. We never had a plan of any kind, nor did we ever think that any removal would be permanent. The Prosecutor adds one sentence to what Mladic says: They will stay there. Because Mladic says: What will happen to a Muslim who goes to Germany? I say: They will remain. It will be regulated by law. I meant he will remain in Republika Srpska because I cannot provide him with residency in Germany. He will be allowed to return. However, they added, the Prosecution added, the word "there." So what is the purpose of this? This would be the destruction of international justice. I am in favour of international justice. There must be courts that would make sure that a criminal who gets into power does not kill people, but it would be a huge failure of that international justice if wrong decisions were made by a court like that. If the reputation of this court is destroyed in small and big nations and among the presidents of those small nations who will one day maybe come here and be in a position to defend themselves for things that they had to do by law and did not commit any crimes. The -- all the documents governing international law are absolutely on our side. Let the Prosecution tell us what other outcome was possible. Did we have any other way out or was it necessary defence? In criminal law, necessary defence is a valid principle. If your safety is threatened, you have to defend yourself. In Sarajevo, in three years, they can show 126 of sniping victims and charge me for that. No, they are showing victims of stray bullets. Thomas Mole and I don't know which other UN officers, all of them say that more people died from stray bullets than from all the sniping. For instance, the 1st Sarajevo Brigade had snipers, but that unit had a front line facing Gorazde, the outer ring, and of course they had snipers. The question is who the snipers were sniping at. They were sniping at other snipers, enemy snipers. To have snipers in itself is not illegal. What's illegal is to shoot at civilians and there is no evidence that they deliberately shot civilians. A stray bullet that hits a tram cannot be viewed as targeting a particular person, especially if the person is sitting behind a not-really-transparent window. To conclude, Your Excellencies, excuse me my amateur approach. I care more about the truth than about the form. I know that justice and law are not always the same thing, but I care more for justice and the truth, and that's why I chose to represent myself, not because I'm such a fool. However, I realised that nobody can defend themselves properly if they are not defended by somebody else. The Defence teams do not have resources to carry out their own proper investigations. We showed you a document dated 4 April which was not found in the case of General Milosevic, and General Fraser admitted it was a document that was an integral part of the orders of the 6th of April. If that document had been produced, Milosevic would not have been convicted of the incident in Hrasnica of the modified air bomb. However, his Defence team did not have sufficient resources to dig into archives. My Defence team is also restricted in personnel and money, but they have unlimited loyalty and dedication and commitment and they dug up far more than any other Defence team before them. I sincerely hope that my accidental improprieties be forgiven. I have participated in this process without any wish to obstruct it, only wishing to get to the truth. The truth will remain and whether the judgement and what's on paper will be along the same lines matters less. In the papers, however, there are enough elements for the truth to be known. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. We'll soon adjourn for the week. Before we resume next Tuesday for rebuttal and rejoinder arguments there are several administrative matters I would like to deal with now. First, the Chamber notes for the purposes of the record its instruction that the parties complete all pending issues related to exhibits by 14th of October, 2014, as conveyed via e-mail from the Chamber's Legal Officer on the 20th of September. Next, the Chamber notes that there are six documents which remain marked for identification in this case. They are: MFI D268, D3536, D4264, D4284, D4288, and D4289. The Chamber recalls its order regarding the close of the Defence case, issued on the 20th of February, 2014, in which the Chamber ordered the parties to file submissions on any exhibit-related matter, including on documents that remained marked for identification, by 17th of March, 2014. Given that this dead-line has passed, the Chamber instructs the Registry to mark those documents, i.e., MFI D268, D3536, D4264, D4284, D4288, and D4289, as marked as not admitted in this case. Finally, before we adjourn, I would like to raise a couple of matters that I would like the Prosecution to address on Tuesday. First, the Chamber noticed in respect of Srebrenica and the joint criminal enterprise to eliminate, the Prosecution final brief refers to the accused's responsibility for deportation under Count 7 as seen, for example, in paragraph 1101 and footnote 3977. On the other hand, in the Defence final brief, the accused notes, relying on paragraph 75 of the indictment, that Count 7 is not charged in relation to Srebrenica as seen in paragraph 3308, in particular footnote 6691. Now, Mr. Tieger, the Chamber notes that this very question was posed to you during the pre-trial proceedings by Lord Bonomy, the then-Presiding Judge of the Pre-Trial Chamber, and that the Prosecution addressed it in its submission on Rule 73 bis, filed on 31st of August, 2009. In paragraph 16 of that submission, the Prosecution explained that deportation was omitted on purpose from paragraph 75 of the indictment and explained that deportation is discussed in paragraph 74 of the indictment only as a means discussed during the formulation of the plan to eliminate the Muslim population from Srebrenica. The Prosecution also crossed out Count 7 in relation to Srebrenica in appendix B of that submission. Thus, from that moment on, both the accused and the Chamber were put on notice that Count 7 is not charged in relation to Srebrenica. I would therefore like you to clarify for the Chamber the brief's reference to Count 7 in relation to Srebrenica. Second, on 10th of September, 2014, the Chamber received the Prosecution's submission with respect to incidents and charges on which no evidence was presented. In this submission, the Prosecution states that after the delivery of the trial judgement, the Prosecution will declare that it will not proceed further with the incidents and charges against the accused which have been excluded pursuant to Rule 73 bis. The Chamber would like to know why the Prosecution cannot make this declaration now so that these charges are withdrawn after the closing arguments but before the judgement is delivered. The hearing is adjourned. We'll resume Tuesday next week.
